full_judgment: 6. In Maritime Electric Co's case, plaintiff company had under-billed the defendant for the electric current supplied by a mistake Later on, the mistake being discovered they made a further demand and succeeded in obtaining a decree. The question was whether they were estopped from demanding the excess amount. The Privy Council observed that the electric company was under a statutory duty to charge full amount for the electricity consumed and the non-user was under an. equal obligation to pay the amount under a statute. The plea of estoppel was not allowed to defeat a statutory obligation which was of an unconditional character. It was observed that in case of a statute enacted for the benefit of a section of the public, i e., on grounds of public policy where the statute imposes a duty of a positive kind for the doing of the very act which the party suing seeks todo, it is not open to the opposite party to setup an estoppel to provent it. In this case the rule of estoppel was not allowed to prevail over the statute because it appeared that if the rule was allowed to prevail it would defeat the public policy of the statute. In the present case, no such question appears to have arisen. There is nothing in the S.A. and T. Act to suggest that the Legislature intended that in case any person sublet his Khas land in contravention of section 75A he would get back his land. Bvidently this could not be the intention if the rule of estoppel is applied against the plaintiff in the present case there is nothing to show that the policy of the statute will be defeated and in that view of the matter the rule laid down in Maritime Electric Company's case is not applicable to the present case.
